🏛️ Virtue Spotlight: Courtesy
When we study the Northeast, we're studying real places and real people. Courtesy means we notice what makes this region interesting and important, not just whether it's somewhere we'd want to visit. The Northeast is not only big cities. It is small fishing towns, farms, and forests too, and the people there are proud of all of it. Every region has its own story worth telling.
🕯️

Where Is the Northeast?
📖
Land, Water, and Weather of the Northeast
A walk through the region before you map it
📖
The Northeast Alcove Opens

The Northeast is in the upper-right corner of the United States, along the Atlantic Ocean. It includes: Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland.

🏔️ The land. The Appalachian Mountains run through much of the Northeast, from Maine down through Pennsylvania. They are very old mountains, so they are lower and rounder than the Rocky Mountains out West. Between the mountains and the ocean, the land gets flatter near the coast. Harbors (deep, calm water where ships can stop safely) made the Northeast a natural place for fishing villages and trading ports.

🌊 The water. The Atlantic Ocean borders the entire eastern side. The Hudson River (New York) and the Delaware River are important waterways. Niagara Falls is in New York, between two of the Great Lakes.

❄️ The climate. The Northeast has four distinct seasons. Winters can be very cold and snowy, especially in New England (Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and Connecticut). Spring is maple sap time. Summers are warm. In fall, the leaves turn red, orange, and gold. Hurricanes sometimes reach the coast.

🦞 Resources. Fishing (especially lobster off the coast of Maine), maple syrup from Vermont, New York, and Maine, coal from Pennsylvania (it powered factories, trains, and homes for more than 100 years), and some of the oldest seaports in the country.

🏙️ Cities. Boston, New York City, Philadelphia, and Baltimore are some of the oldest and largest cities in the country. They grew up near harbors because trade and shipping were easy. Long ago, millions of newcomers to the United States arrived at Ellis Island, near the Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor. New York City is the biggest city in the country, but it is not the capital. The capital of the United States is Washington, D.C.

🌲 Not just cities. Most of the Northeast is not big cities. It also has thick forests, mountain farms, apple orchards, and small fishing towns along a rocky coast.

🦸

Northeast Hero: Jackie Robinson served in the U.S. Army. Then in 1947, in Brooklyn, New York, he became the first African American to play in modern Major League Baseball. Some fans were cruel to him, but he kept playing with courage and helped open the game to everyone.

⏳

Then & Now: Long ago, the Northeast's harbors made it the center of trade. Ships loaded with fish, lumber, and goods sailed out to Europe and the Caribbean. Today those same harbors are used for shipping containers, cruise ships, and fishing boats. What stayed the same about why the Northeast's coast matters?

🤔

Pause & Think: If you visited the Northeast, would you head for the rocky coastline of Maine, the Appalachian Mountains in Vermont, or the streets of New York City? Why?

🔎 Discovery Fact
The Boston Post Road was one of the first major roads in the United States. It was used in the 1600s and 1700s to carry mail between Boston and New York City. Today, the highway U.S. Route 1 follows much of the same route!
📷

Source: One Harbor, 100 Years Apart

Look closely. What changed in New York Harbor? What stayed the same? Why did a big city grow right here?

The Big Picture
🏷️ Exhibit Label

The Northeast region sits in the upper-right corner of the United States, along the Atlantic Ocean. It has the Appalachian Mountains, four clear seasons, and some of the oldest cities in the country. From fishing villages in Maine to the skyscrapers of New York City, the Northeast is shaped by its coastline, its mountains, and its long history.

🦉
🧭 Opti says…
The Appalachian Mountains are some of the oldest mountains on Earth, much older than the Rockies out West! They've been worn down by millions of years of wind and rain. Long ago, before the dinosaurs, they may have been as tall as the Rockies are today!

The Northeast is coming into focus. Let's check what you remember before you fill the alcove.

🧠
Quick Self-Check
🧠

Not graded. Just for you! Answer these three questions before you fill the Northeast alcove.

1. Where is the Northeast region on a map of the United States?
AIn the upper-right corner, along the Atlantic Ocean
BIn the lower-left corner
CIn the middle of the country
Yes! The Northeast runs from Maine down to Maryland, along the Atlantic coast.
Think about the crate map. The Northeast is near the Atlantic Ocean. Try again!
2. What mountain range runs through the Northeast?
AThe Rocky Mountains
BThe Cascade Mountains
CThe Appalachian Mountains
Yes! The Appalachians run through the Northeast. They are so old that they are low and rounded.
The Rockies and the Cascades are in the West. Which old, rounded mountains did we study today?
3. Which resource did people dig out of the ground in Pennsylvania for many years?
AGold
BCoal
CCotton
Yes! Pennsylvania coal powered factories, trains, and homes for more than 100 years.
Gold was found in California, and cotton grows in the warm Southeast. Think about the black rock in the crate.
